summary:
ASTRA is an innovative astronaut assistance concept designed to support health awareness and situational awareness during long-duration space missions. Developed in response to the NASA Space Apps Challenge, “Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions,” ASTRA brings together an immersive astronaut-view interface, a Heads-Up Display (HUD)-inspired visualization, and a Mission Control dashboard.

The platform explores how astronauts and mission teams could access important health-related information, mission status, and emergency alerts through an integrated digital interface. Its smartphone-based camera system demonstrates an astronaut's point of view, while the web dashboard illustrates how health information and alerts could be presented to mission control.

ASTRA addresses the challenges of isolation, limited medical assistance, and continuous health awareness in space. Our current prototype demonstrates the concept using simulated health data, with real-time biometric sensors and intelligent health analysis planned for future development.

Our vision is to make astronaut health monitoring more accessible, intuitive, and intelligent through affordable technology and human-centered design.
details:
ASTRA – Astronaut Health Monitoring & Immersive Vision System

ASTRA is a prototype concept designed to support astronaut health awareness and situational awareness during long-duration space missions. It combines an immersive astronaut-view interface with a Mission Control dashboard to demonstrate how health-related information can be presented in a simple and accessible way.

The prototype uses a smartphone camera mounted inside a cardboard astronaut helmet to demonstrate an astronaut's point of view. A browser-based camera interface displays the live camera feed with a Heads-Up Display (HUD)-inspired visual overlay. A separate Mission Control dashboard presents a visualization of astronaut health information and mission-related alerts, helping demonstrate how crew health status could be monitored and communicated.

The project aims to address challenges associated with long-duration missions, including isolation, limited access to immediate medical assistance, and the need for continuous health awareness. Its intended impact is to explore a more intuitive and accessible way for astronauts and mission-support teams to understand health-related information.

Tools and Technologies Used: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, TypeScript, smartphone camera, browser camera APIs, Odoo Website Builder, and AI-assisted development tools. The prototype was developed using a combination of web technologies and a low-cost physical helmet mock-up.

Creativity and Innovation: ASTRA brings together an astronaut-perspective camera experience, HUD-style interface, and Mission Control dashboard in one concept. Instead of presenting health information only through conventional charts, it explores how information could be displayed within an astronaut-oriented visual environment.

Design Considerations: Our team considered usability, readability, low-cost prototyping, astronaut perspective, accessibility of information, and the challenges of operating in isolated space environments.

Current Prototype Limitations: Health readings and alerts displayed on the dashboard are simulated demonstration data. Real biometric sensor integration, validated medical analysis, and operational spaceflight hardware are not yet implemented. AST
